To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nuclear Cdx2 is expressed not only at the intestinal epithelium but also in other organs, including the gallbladder.

nuclear Cdx2 immunostaining is observed in a variety of tumours, and that this expression correlates with morular differentiation, which is a histological feature of intestinal differentiation, and with nuclear accumulation of b‐catenin, which is a key factor for Wnt signalling.
aberrant nuclear Cdx expression in morule-forming tumours in different sites is accompanied by cytoplamic reactivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Cdx2 expression pattern in morule-forming tumours of various organs, and with its relationship to nuclear b-catenin and MUC2.
the expression of Cdx1 and Cdx2 in normal and neoplastic epithelium of the human stomach and colon.
the aberrant expression of the Cdx2 gene in the morule-forming tumours in different sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nuclear Cdx2 immunostaining is a useful marker for intestinal differentiation in the gastrointestinal tract and female genital tract, and is also useful for the differential diagnosis of intestinal and endometrioid neoplasms.
nuclear expression of Cdx-2 is a reliable marker for intestinal metaplasias in the gastrointestinal tract, whereas its expression in the cytoplasm is nonspecific.
Cdx2 immunohistochemical staining is useful in detecting the morule‐forming component of tumours in the stomach, pancreatobiliary system, and female genital tract.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nuclear Cdx2 is a marker of intestinal metaplasialike changes in the gallbladder.
Cdx2 is a useful marker in the differential diagnosis between intestinal and non-intestinal endometrioid carcinomas.
nuclear Cdx2 is a useful marker for the identification of morule‐forming adenocarcinomata in various organs and cytoplasmic expression is not a useful marker for this purpose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Cdx2 is expressed in morule-forming tumors of various organs, and this aberrant expression is associated with nuclear accumulation of b- catenin.
Cdx2 is not a specific marker for intestinal differentiation.
Cdx2 immunoreactivity is not a specific marker of intestinal differentiation in the female genital tract or in other organs.
